author: Orienta
name: Find the particles in a single-metal matrix
notes:
Groups the map into chemically distinct areas and names them from your CIF library.

GOOD FOR: precipitates and inclusions a few micrometres across in a single-metal matrix - steel, copper, nickel, aluminium.
NOT FOR: layered samples or heavily mixed microstructures, where "matrix plus particles" is the wrong picture to start from.

This is a sensible starting point you can then correct. It is not the correct answer.

NO MATRIX ELEMENT IS PINNED, so the matrix is inferred from each scan (the element above ~40 at%). That is the convenient choice and the fragile one: enrichment is measured against the matrix, and getting it wrong inverts the measure. On your own material, save a copy with your matrix element pinned - the compatibility check can then refuse a scan it does not fit instead of quietly measuring against the wrong baseline.

SMOOTHING is 2.5 um, a physical width, so it means the same analysis at any step size. Measured on the SampleB test scan (0.5 um step): a 5 px box, 7 distinct areas, coherence 0.933. Features thinner than the box are absorbed - lower it for finer particles, raise it for noisier maps.

CANDIDATE PHASES are whatever your CIF library holds; this preset pins no list, so it is convenient and not reproducible. Pin the list in your own copy.
